title: Fundamental Skills for Data Science
officialDescription: Establishes background knowledge in Python and R programming, multivariate calculus and linear algebra, and basic statistics to prepare incoming students for success in the core courses in the M.S. in Data Science Program.
studentDescription: Build a shared foundation in programming, mathematics, and statistical thinking for the rest of the curriculum.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open only to students in the Data Science M.S. program.
sourceNotes: The MSDS course page calls this Fundamentals of Data Science. The 2026–2027 Graduate Catalog title, Fundamental Skills for Data Science, is used here.

title: Applied Statistics for Data Science
officialDescription: Statistics essential for data science incorporating descriptive statistics; integrative numerical description and visualization of data; graphical methods for determining and comparing distributions of data; data-driven statistical inference of one-sample, two-sample, and k-sample problems; linear regression; non-linear regression; and dependent data models.
studentDescription: Develop applied statistical reasoning and modeling to connect data with evidence and uncertainty.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: GRAD 5100, may be taken concurrently; Open only to MS Data Science students, others with instructor consent. Recommended preparation: An undergraduate course in statistics. Not open for credit to students who have passed BIST/STAT 5505 or BIST/STAT 5605.
sourceNotes: The current catalog requires GRAD 5100, which may be taken concurrently, and states the current enrollment and credit restrictions. This differs from the older prerequisite wording on the MSDS course page; catalog requirements are preserved here.

title: Statistical Computing for Data Science
officialDescription: Principles and practice of statistical computing in data science: data structure, distributed computing and project management tools, data visualization, and data programming including simulation, resampling methods, and applications of optimization for statistical modeling, inference, and prediction. Formerly offered as STAT 5125.
studentDescription: Strengthen the computational toolkit that turns statistical ideas into reproducible analyses.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: GRAD 5100 and STAT 5405; Open only to MS Data Science students, others with instructor consent.
sourceNotes: The current catalog requires GRAD 5100 and STAT 5405. This differs from the older prerequisite wording on the MSDS course page; catalog requirements are preserved here.

title: Machine Learning for Data Science
officialDescription: An introduction to the techniques of machine learning, including models for both supervised and unsupervised learning, and related optimization techniques, covering topics such as regression, neural networks, clustering, model evaluation and selection, and implementation of learning algorithms from first principles.
studentDescription: Understand the learning foundations behind predictive models and modern AI tools.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: GRAD 5100; Open to graduate students in the M.S. in Data Science program. Recommended preparation: Python programming, multivariable calculus, linear algebra, introductory statistics.

title: Data Mining for Data Science
officialDescription: This course presents an introduction to data mining algorithms in the areas of classification, association analysis, clustering, and anomaly detection, with an emphasis on a conceptual understanding these algorithms along with their application in real-world problems and domains.
studentDescription: Connect data-mining methods with the practical task of finding useful patterns in data.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: CSE 5709; Open to graduate students in the M.S. in Data Science program. Recommended preparation: Python programming including open-source libraries: scikit-learn, Numpy, Matplotlib, introductory statistics

title: Causal Inference and Measurement for Data Science
officialDescription: Principles and practice of causal inference and measurement for data scientists. Topics include: fundamentals of causal inference, establishing causal (rather than correlational) relationships -- via AB tests, controlling for confounders, and the use of panel data -- and the fundamentals of measurement. Validity and reproducibility are themes throughout the course.
studentDescription: Reason about causal questions, measurement, and evaluation beyond predictive association.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open to students enrolled in the M.S. Data Science program or with instructor consent. Recommended preparation: Knowledge of Introductory inferential and descriptive statistics.

title: Data Ethics and Equity in the Era of Misinformation
officialDescription: This course will introduce students to issues of ethics and equity in the contemporary practice of data science. The ability to collect, store, process, and analyze ever greater amounts of data offers great opportunities, as well as potential perils. This course will provide examine the ethical implications of data collection, usage, and distribution. Topics will include systematic approaches to assessing ethical issues; privacy and confidentiality; defining research and the responsibilities associated with conducting ethical research; implicit and structural biases in data collection and analysis.
studentDescription: Examine the ethical and equity questions that arise when data informs decisions and public understanding.

title: Data Visualization and Communication
officialDescription: Data visualization is a form of storytelling that provides an effective way to draw conclusions and share insights, allowing people to express big, complex ideas in simple ways. Utilizing state of the art software, the use of parameters, filters, calculated variables, color, space and motion to visually articulate the data are surveyed. Common pitfalls and ethics issues in visualization design are also considered. This interactive course is designed to help students learn the methods, tools, and techniques to best understand and present complex data so that they can persuasively share results and influence decisions.
studentDescription: Develop visual and communication approaches that make analytical evidence understandable and useful.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Open only to M.S. Data Science students; others with consent.

title: Applied Capstone in Data Science
officialDescription: This course will give M.S. in Data Science students a problem-based learning opportunity to apply knowledge and skills gained in core and elective courses to an integrative data science project. Projects for the course come from industry and program partners and will typically require students to work in small teams to solve a real-world data science problem.
studentDescription: Integrate the curriculum through a real-world applied project with a question, an analysis, and a useful outcome.
prerequisites: Enrollment Requirements: Enrollment in the M.S. in Data Science program; Department or Unit consent required. Recommended preparation: Nine credits of coursework required for the M.S. in Data Science.
